indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B4.4.2.1 Demonstrate knowledge of generation of electricity, its transmission and transformation into other forms

skills.description: Explain simply what conserving electricity means (using less and avoiding waste).
List ways to conserve electricity (switching off lights, using energy-efficient bulbs, unplugging appliances).
Recognise actions that waste electricity (leaving lights on, appliances on standby).
State why conserving electricity is important (saves money, reduces waste).
Suggest conservation actions for home and school.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Leaving appliances on standby does not waste electricity.
Turning off lights does not save electricity.
Conserving electricity means not using it at all.
Electricity is free, so there is no need to conserve it.

questions.stem: What does conserving electricity mean?
options: Using more electricity
Using electricity wisely and avoiding waste
Never using electricity
Buying more appliances
hints: Conserving means saving.
You still use electricity, but you do not waste it.
questions.explanation: Conserving electricity means using it wisely and avoiding waste. It does not mean never using electricity.
questions.misconception: Conserving electricity means not using it at all.

questions.stem: Which of these helps to conserve electricity?
options: Leaving lights on all day
Switching off lights when leaving a room
Turning on all appliances at once
Leaving the television on when nobody is watching
hints: Which action saves electricity?
Switching off unused lights saves power.
questions.explanation: Switching off lights when leaving a room conserves electricity. Leaving them on wastes electricity.
questions.misconception: Leaving lights on does not waste electricity.

questions.stem: Which of these actions wastes electricity?
options: Switching off the fan when leaving the room
Unplugging the phone charger after use
Leaving the television on when nobody is watching
Turning off the light during the day
hints: Which action uses electricity for no reason?
If nobody is watching, the TV is wasting power.
questions.explanation: Leaving the television on when nobody is watching wastes electricity. The other actions conserve electricity.
questions.misconception: Leaving appliances on does not waste electricity.

questions.stem: Why should we conserve electricity?
options: To make the house darker
To save money and reduce waste
To make appliances break
To use more power
hints: Electricity costs money.
Saving electricity saves money.
questions.explanation: Conserving electricity saves money on electricity bills and reduces waste of energy.
questions.misconception: Electricity is free, so there is no need to conserve it.

questions.stem: What can pupils do at school to conserve electricity?
options: Leave classroom lights on after school
Switch off lights when leaving the classroom
Turn on all fans and leave them on
Leave computers on all night
hints: What should you do when you leave a room?
Turning off lights saves electricity.
questions.explanation: Switching off classroom lights when leaving helps conserve electricity at school.
questions.misconception: Pupils cannot help conserve electricity.

questions.stem: Which of these is a good way to conserve electricity at home?
options: Leaving the iron on after use
Using energy-efficient bulbs
Keeping all lights on at night
Leaving the fridge door open
hints: Energy-efficient bulbs use less power.
They save electricity compared to ordinary bulbs.
questions.explanation: Energy-efficient bulbs use less electricity than ordinary bulbs. They help conserve electricity.
questions.misconception: All bulbs use the same amount of electricity.

questions.stem: Ama leaves her phone charger plugged in even after her phone is fully charged. Is this a good practice?
options: Yes, it charges the phone faster
Yes, it does not matter
No, it wastes electricity
No, it makes the phone cold
hints: Does a charger use electricity when the phone is full?
Unplugging saves electricity.
questions.explanation: Leaving a charger plugged in when the phone is fully charged wastes electricity. Unplugging it helps conserve electricity.
questions.misconception: Leaving appliances on standby does not waste electricity.

questions.stem: What should you do to conserve electricity when you are the last person to leave the classroom?
options: Close the windows
Sweep the floor
Switch off the lights and fans
Open the door
hints: What uses electricity in the classroom?
Turn off what is not needed.
questions.explanation: Switching off the lights and fans when leaving the classroom conserves electricity.
questions.misconception: Lights and fans do not need to be switched off.

questions.stem: Which of these should a family do to conserve electricity at home?
options: Leave the television on all night
Use natural light during the day instead of electric lights
Keep all lights on in every room
Leave the fridge door open
hints: The sun gives light during the day.
Why use electric lights when the sun is shining?
questions.explanation: Using natural light from the sun during the day reduces the need for electric lights, conserving electricity.
questions.misconception: Electric lights should be on all day.

questions.stem: What does it mean to conserve electricity?
answer: to use electricity wisely and avoid wasting it
to use less electricity and not waste it
using electricity carefully without wasting it
hints: Conserving means saving.
Do not waste electricity.
questions.explanation: Conserving electricity means using it wisely and avoiding waste. It does not mean never using electricity.
questions.misconception: Conserving electricity means not using it at all.

questions.stem: Which is a reason for conserving electricity?
options: To reduce electricity bills
To make appliances stop working
To make the house darker
To use more energy
hints: Electricity bills cost money.
Using less electricity saves money.
questions.explanation: Conserving electricity reduces electricity bills because less power is used.
questions.misconception: Electricity is free, so there is no need to conserve it.

questions.stem: Give one example of an action that wastes electricity.
answer: leaving lights on when leaving a room
leaving the television on when nobody is watching
leaving the fan on when not in the room
leaving the charger plugged in after the phone is charged
hints: Think of something left on with no one using it.
Leaving lights on is one example.
questions.explanation: Actions like leaving lights on, leaving the TV on when nobody is watching, or leaving appliances on standby all waste electricity.
questions.misconception: Leaving lights on does not waste electricity.

questions.stem: State two reasons why conserving electricity is important.
answer: it saves money and reduces waste
it saves money and helps protect the environment
it reduces electricity bills and prevents waste of energy
hints: Electricity costs money.
Wasting electricity wastes resources.
questions.explanation: Conserving electricity saves money on bills and reduces waste of energy resources, which is good for the environment.
questions.misconception: Conserving electricity is not important.

questions.stem: List two ways of conserving electricity at home.
answer: switch off lights when leaving a room and unplug appliances when not in use
use energy-efficient bulbs and switch off unused appliances
turn off lights during the day and unplug chargers after use
hints: What should you do with lights when leaving a room?
What should you do with appliances not in use?
questions.explanation: Ways to conserve electricity include switching off lights when leaving a room, unplugging appliances when not in use, using energy-efficient bulbs, and using natural light during the day.
questions.misconception: There is no way to conserve electricity.

questions.stem: Suggest one way pupils can help conserve electricity at school.
answer: switch off lights and fans when leaving the classroom
turn off lights when not needed
unplug appliances when not in use
hints: What uses electricity in the classroom?
Turn them off when not needed.
questions.explanation: Pupils can help conserve electricity by switching off lights and fans when leaving the classroom or when they are not needed.
questions.misconception: Pupils cannot help conserve electricity.

questions.stem: Which of these actions conserves electricity?
options: Leaving the TV on standby all night
Using natural light during the day
Keeping all lights on in the house
Leaving the iron on after use
hints: The sun gives light during the day.
Using sunlight saves electricity.
questions.explanation: Using natural light during the day conserves electricity. The other actions waste electricity.
questions.misconception: Using natural light does not save electricity.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'Conserving electricity means never using electricity at all.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, that is correct
No, conserving means using electricity wisely without wasting it
No, conserving means using more electricity
No, conserving means buying more appliances
hints: Can you live without electricity entirely?
Conserving is about avoiding waste, not avoiding use.
questions.explanation: Conserving electricity means using it wisely and avoiding waste. It does not mean never using electricity.
questions.misconception: Conserving electricity means not using it at all.

questions.stem: A family leaves all their lights, fans, and television on even when they go out. What is the effect of this?
options: It saves electricity
It wastes electricity and increases their bill
It makes the house cooler
It charges their appliances
hints: If nobody is home, are the appliances needed?
Leaving them on wastes power.
questions.explanation: Leaving appliances on when nobody is home wastes electricity and increases the electricity bill.
questions.misconception: Leaving appliances on does not waste electricity.

questions.stem: A pupil wants to help their family conserve electricity. Which plan is BEST?
options: Leave all lights on at night
Switch off unused lights and unplug appliances not in use
Use more appliances every day
Leave the fridge door open to keep the kitchen cool
hints: Which plan avoids waste?
Switching off and unplugging saves electricity.
questions.explanation: Switching off unused lights and unplugging appliances not in use is the best plan for conserving electricity at home.
questions.misconception: Leaving appliances on does not waste electricity.

questions.stem: Why is conserving electricity important for the whole country, not just for one family?
options: It helps the country save energy resources and reduces the cost of electricity for everyone
It makes the country darker
It stops people from using electricity
It makes appliances last longer
hints: Electricity is generated using resources.
If everyone conserves, less energy is wasted.
questions.explanation: Conserving electricity helps the whole country save energy resources and reduces the cost of generating and supplying electricity, which benefits everyone.
questions.misconception: Conserving electricity only benefits one person.
